h: Potteries pointers for a smooth climb
p: Like most fun-climbing centres, Clip 'n Climb works on booked sessions, so get your slot reserved before you set off and plan on a couple of hours for the full visit. That covers arriving, getting harnessed up, the safety briefing and your time on the walls.

Paperwork next. Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's far quicker done online at home. The age guidance is worth a look when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for little ones.

Got a nervous climber? Let them watch a couple of people come down first, then start them on a low wall with an early let-go. Once they've felt how gently the auto-belay lowers them, the confidence usually comes flooding in. Trainers, comfy clothes and a water bottle are all you need.

There's plenty in the area to make a proper day of it. The Trentham Estate, on the southern edge of Stoke-on-Trent, has beautiful gardens, a lake, a shopping village and Trentham Monkey Forest, where Barbary macaques roam free in the woodland. Gladstone Pottery Museum in Longton is a brilliant, hands-on look at the bottle kilns and working lives of the Potteries, and the World of Wedgwood at Barlaston lets you see pottery being made and have a go yourself. All three are a fairly short drive from Stone.
